correctness.rationale: The known minimum domination 3-set classification is reconstructed with its quantifiers for n>=5; triangle isolation follows from two-edge overlap. Matchings have jump/slide degree 3*(C(n-4,2)-1) and 3*C(n-6,2). One free ground point suffices to insert any fixed target matching edge using one/two jumps, proving jumping connectivity for n>=7. At n=8 a sliding move preserves the eight-point four-pair partition, giving exactly 105 K4; at n>=9 every incident-endpoint jump is simulated by two legal slides using two other free endpoints. Direct full domination brute force through n=10 and independent C++ matching enumeration through n=11 confirm all base and boundary cases. Finite tests are supplemental, not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: A natural infinite-parameter family of standard Kneser graphs exhibits a sharp difference between canonical reconfiguration rules: the same optimal matching solutions are frozen at n=7 in sliding despite moving by jumps, split into exactly 105 K4 at n=8, and become globally connected at n=9. The proof isolates a structural conserved perfect matching and supplies constructive simulations; these determine genuine optimal-solution mobility barriers, not numerical table increments or a rephrased minimum-size fact.
